title: Detecting and monitoring long-term landslides in urbanized areas with nighttime light data and multi-seasonal Landsat imagery across Taiwan from 1998 to 2017
datasets: NASA SRTM 30 m Digital Elevation Model

dataset_roles.dataset: NASA SRTM 30 m Digital Elevation Model

idea.research_question: Can medium-resolution optical imagery identify long-term landslides in urbanized terrain when human activity creates spectral confounders?
idea.hypothesis: Seasonal optical trajectories detect exposed landslide material, nighttime radiance separates anthropogenic disturbance, and terrain features reduce classification ambiguity.
idea.mechanism: Random-forest classification, multi-season compositing, independent validation and long-term recurrence mapping
idea.expected_contribution: Transfers a human-activity proxy into natural-hazard disambiguation.
idea.falsification_condition: Reject if any required role is omitted, background-only, or not operationally used in the same research instance.

anchor_context.extraction_basis: Full-text seed evidence; empirical results are excluded from the task prompt.
